I can jump on a call now if helpful — Alan (CTO)

Folks — forwarding what Alan sent. Initial findings from infra: we see a burst-credit imbalance on the customer’s tenant starting 09:00:55. The safety-valve (burst credits) were drained quickly due to a high-concurrency prefix rewrite the customer runs during their nightly job. That caused rapid fallback to stricter per-route governors.

What I’m asking Ops to do now:
1) Snapshot quota and burst allocations (attached: quota-config-snapshot-20290802.json).
2) Temporarily raise MediProbe’s burst allowance and relax the guardrail on the ingestion route to prevent further rejections while we investigate root cause.
3) Replay the last 10 minutes of requests in a staging sandbox to validate behavior before prod change.

Risk note: increasing burst allowance will raise short-term token cost, but keeps product availability. Need exec sign-off for a sustained policy change.

Attaching: mediprobe-prod-logs-20290802.zip (redwood-infra traces), quota-config-snapshot-20290802.json

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Director, Serving Reliability
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alan King <alan.king@mediprobe.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Aug 2029 09:47:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 429s starting 09:02 PST — urgent

Karthik / Priya — good triage. Quick operational thoughts:
- From the logs: concurrent prefix rewrite caused large KV cache churn and a spike in sustained concurrency for a small subset of tokens. The routing layer credits burst to tenants but we also have a safety cap per tenant-route that prevented the temporary borrow. That mismatch (global burst pool vs per-route cap) is the “guardrail imbalance” — a policy gap where the global pool permitted burst but route-specific caps still enforced hard rejects.

Immediate plan (doing now):
1) Ops will temporarily bump MediProbe route cap from 250 concurrent to 800 for the next 30 minutes and re-enable prefix-borrowing logic suppressed by the last config push.
2) We’ll enable a short-lived adaptive fallback to the compat model for high-latency requests so we return lower-latency responses rather than 429s.
3) Engineering will codify a small hotfix to ensure the global burst pool honors route caps in the allocation decision (prevents oscillation).

Marissa will coordinate the exec note. Priya please keep MediProbe updated and log acceptance of the temporary change in SUP-8341.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | VP, Product Operations
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alan King <alan.king@mediprobe.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Aug 2029 11:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 429s starting 09:02 PST — urgent

Alan — update: we identified a policy mismatch between the global burst allocator and per-route caps that caused your tenant’s burst credits to be effectively unreachable during the scheduled job. Ops applied a short window fix at 09:50 PST: we temporarily increased your ingestion route cap and enabled adaptive fallback to a lower-latency compat model while we implement a durable allocator fix. After the change, errors dropped from ~15% to <1% and latency returned to baseline.

Next steps and ask:
- We will roll a permanent fix to the allocation decision in the next 36 hours (INF-8796) and run a controlled replay of your nightly job in our staging replay environment.
- Please confirm whether MediProbe wants us to keep a higher burst allocation for the remainder of this week while we complete the fix (tradeoff: availability vs. temporary spend).
- I’ve attached the logs and quota snapshot for your review.

Thanks for the quick heads-up. Let me know if you’d like a postmortem and a short exec-level summary once we close INF-8796.

— Priya
